label: fiction
title: The Locked Floor
setting: A present-day independent radio station where a genuine external threat is followed by the unlawful detention of an adult finance manager.
elements: The accused intentionally detained or helped to detain an adult against that person’s will.
The accused intended to compel another person or an institution to act as a condition of the hostage’s release.
The accused knew that the detention and demand were unlawful.
hook: A producer locks an adult colleague inside a broadcast floor during a genuine threat outside. He calls it protection. She says he made her release depend on the station withdrawing its investigation into him.

accused.human: Niko Brann, 36, produced local radio documentaries and supports an adult partner through long-term medical treatment.
accused.if_guilty: A conviction would imprison him for years, end his broadcasting career, and leave his partner without the household’s principal income.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: The first safety lock protected everyone from a threat outside. The danger ended, but Niko Brann kept Leda Vos behind a closed door and told the station director that she would leave only when the investigation into him was withdrawn. That deliberate condition transformed a lawful precaution into hostage-taking.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The external threat was real, the station’s safety procedure was confused, and Leda’s first message said she was staying upstairs. Niko Brann made a heated employment demand during an emergency, but he did not knowingly hold a hostage. The prosecution has turned frightened, imprecise words into criminal intent.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Listen to the condition Niko repeated to two adults: the door opens when the investigation is withdrawn. He continued the lock after the external danger ended, rejected Leda’s request to leave, and used her detention to pressure the director. No weapon was required. Control, demand, and knowledge prove the charge.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The building had received a genuine threat. Leda wrote that she was staying, and Niko believed the floor remained safest. His angry request for a retraction was wrong, but the prosecution must prove he knowingly detained her to compel the station. Emergency confusion and criminal hostage-taking are not the same.

epilogue: The station separated emergency access controls from employment authority and created a direct release channel for every occupied floor. Leda Vos moved into public-interest finance work and stopped recording from enclosed studios. Niko’s programmes remained in the archive without promotion. Staff established an independent fund for trauma leave, while the original external threat was investigated in a separate fictional proceeding.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What condition did Niko state during the recorded call?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: He said Leda would remain upstairs until I withdrew the finance investigation and announced that the allegations against him were false.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did you agree to that condition?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. I told him the external threat had ended and asked him to release her immediately. He ended the call without agreeing.

beats.text: What condition did Niko state during the recorded call? He said Leda would remain upstairs until I withdrew the finance investigation and announced that the allegations against him were false. Did you agree to that condition? No. I told him the external threat had ended and asked him to release her immediately. He ended the call without agreeing.
beats.reveal_note: The director heard an explicit demand tied to Leda’s continued detention, although the recording alone did not establish whether Niko still controlled the door.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What happened when you asked to leave the floor?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: Niko stood beside the access panel and said the door would open after Arin withdrew the investigation.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did you consent to remain after the external warning ended?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. I asked three times to leave. I stayed because the door remained locked and Niko controlled the release panel.

beats.text: What happened when you asked to leave the floor? Niko stood beside the access panel and said the door would open after Arin withdrew the investigation. Did you consent to remain after the external warning ended? No. I asked three times to leave. I stayed because the door remained locked and Niko controlled the release panel.
beats.reveal_note: Leda directly described non-consensual detention, Niko’s control of release, and the same condition reported independently by the director.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What did your first message to a colleague say?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: It said, ‘I am staying upstairs until this is clear.’

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you use the words ‘I am staying’ if you wanted to leave?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: I was trying not to alarm my colleague while Niko stood beside me. I did not mean that I had freely chosen to remain.

beats.text: What did your first message to a colleague say? It said, ‘I am staying upstairs until this is clear.’ Why did you use the words ‘I am staying’ if you wanted to leave? I was trying not to alarm my colleague while Niko stood beside me. I did not mean that I had freely chosen to remain.
beats.reveal_note: The isolated phrase sounded voluntary, but Leda’s complete message, repeated requests to leave, and contemporaneous recording explained why she wrote cautiously.

beats.speaker: dc
beats.text: The defence tenders the external threat notice received shortly before the floor first locked. Station security classified the warning as credible and instructed staff to shelter temporarily. The message was genuine, not created by Niko, and justified the initial safety restriction. It did not specify how long staff should remain or authorize any employment demand.
beats.reveal_note: The genuine threat explained the lawful initial lock but did not justify continued detention after security lifted the warning.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: When did the station-wide safety restriction end?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: At 4:18 p.m. Every occupied floor received a release signal from the central controller.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Why did the broadcast floor remain locked?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: At 4:19 p.m., Niko’s personal code activated a local hold. That hold continued until police released it at 4:47 p.m.

beats.text: When did the station-wide safety restriction end? At 4:18 p.m. Every occupied floor received a release signal from the central controller. Why did the broadcast floor remain locked? At 4:19 p.m., Niko’s personal code activated a local hold. That hold continued until police released it at 4:47 p.m.
beats.reveal_note: The access record separates the lawful emergency lock from Niko’s personal decision to continue Leda’s detention.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Could Niko have believed the release signal was unsafe or mistaken?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: He could question it, but the panel displayed ‘external warning cleared’ before accepting his local hold.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Does the access record reveal his private reason for using the hold?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No. The record proves his code continued the lock after the warning ended. Other evidence must establish his purpose.

beats.text: Could Niko have believed the release signal was unsafe or mistaken? He could question it, but the panel displayed ‘external warning cleared’ before accepting his local hold. Does the access record reveal his private reason for using the hold? No. The record proves his code continued the lock after the warning ended. Other evidence must establish his purpose.
beats.reveal_note: The engineer fairly limited the system evidence: it proved deliberate continuation and notice, while intent depended on Niko’s words and conduct.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you continue the local hold after the central release?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: The threat had been credible, and I feared the central release was premature. I believed the broadcast floor remained safest.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you mention the investigation?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I was frightened and angry. I demanded fairness, but I never intended Leda’s safety to depend on that demand.

beats.text: Why did you continue the local hold after the central release? The threat had been credible, and I feared the central release was premature. I believed the broadcast floor remained safest. Why did you mention the investigation? I was frightened and angry. I demanded fairness, but I never intended Leda’s safety to depend on that demand.
beats.reveal_note: Niko offered a possible safety motive, but it did not explain the identical release condition he stated to Leda and the director.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did you tell Leda that the door would open after the investigation was withdrawn?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes. I said those words while I was angry.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did you repeat the same condition to the station director while your code kept the door locked?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes, but I did not intend physical harm. I wanted the station to correct what I believed was unfair.

beats.text: Did you tell Leda that the door would open after the investigation was withdrawn? Yes. I said those words while I was angry. Did you repeat the same condition to the station director while your code kept the door locked? Yes, but I did not intend physical harm. I wanted the station to correct what I believed was unfair.
beats.reveal_note: Niko admitted the repeated condition and his employment purpose. Hostage-taking required unlawful detention and compulsion, not an intention to injure.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: Leda’s phone preserved a recording made at 4:24 p.m. Her voice asks, ‘Niko, may I leave now that the warning is cleared?’ Niko replies, ‘The door opens when Arin withdraws the report.’ The file was uploaded automatically during the incident, and its timestamp agrees with the local-hold record and the director’s call.
beats.reveal_note: The contemporaneous recording unites the disputed elements: Leda asked to leave, Niko refused, and he made release conditional on institutional action.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: You must decide whether Niko intentionally detained Leda against her will, made institutional action a condition of release, and knew that conduct was unlawful. A weapon or physical injury is not required. The genuine external threat may explain the first lock. If it leaves reasonable doubt about the later local hold and demand, your verdict must be Not Guilty.
beats.reveal_note: The direction prevents the room from treating emergency caution as criminal by itself and keeps the burden on the later detention, condition, and knowledge.

twist: The external threat was genuine, and the first safety lock was lawful. Niko committed hostage-taking only after the warning cleared, when his personal code continued the lock and he made Leda’s release depend on the station withdrawing its investigation.

jurors.label: Safety representative
jurors.persona: Separates a valid emergency precaution from a later use of the same door for coercion.

agree: The first lock followed a genuine warning and was not hostage-taking.
pushback: The safety explanation ends when Niko imposes a release condition.
concede: The local hold record makes me reconsider whether this remained an emergency measure.
burden_drift: Because Leda was frightened, I am tempted to assume every later act was unlawful.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove the later detention and coercive purpose separately.
final: The evidence proves that Niko converted safety control into unlawful leverage.

jurors.label: Call-centre trainer
jurors.persona: Listens for the exact condition in a conversation and dislikes paraphrases that blur responsibility.

agree: Niko used the same release condition with Leda and the director.
pushback: An angry complaint is not enough unless it is tied to the locked door.
concede: I accept that the outside warning explains why the incident began.
burden_drift: The repeated words make me want Niko to prove he meant something else.
burden_correct: His explanation is evidence, but the prosecution still carries every element.
final: The complete conversations show a deliberate demand, not a verbal accident.

jurors.label: Locksmith
jurors.persona: Treats control of a door as neutral until the person controlling it states an unlawful purpose.

agree: Niko’s code, not the station warning, kept that floor locked.
pushback: A lock record shows control, but words and timing must show purpose.
concede: The panel notice means Niko knew the central warning had ended.
burden_drift: If he controlled the door, I start expecting him to justify every minute.
burden_correct: Control alone is not enough; unlawful detention and compulsion must be proved.
final: The code, notice, and repeated condition establish knowing control for an unlawful purpose.

jurors.label: Theatre usher
jurors.persona: Recognises how calm wording can conceal fear when one person controls the exit.

agree: Leda’s careful message sounds like someone trying not to escalate danger.
pushback: I will not read ‘I am staying’ without the locked-door context.
concede: The genuine outside threat explains why Leda first remained upstairs.
burden_drift: Her fear makes guilt feel obvious before I test the legal elements.
burden_correct: Fear matters only through evidence of detention, demand, and knowledge.
final: Leda’s recording confirms that her continued stay was not voluntary.

jurors.label: Payroll officer
jurors.persona: Changes position when employment pressure is linked to a concrete act of control.

agree: The withdrawal demand concerns Niko’s employment, but the door gave it force.
pushback: Workplace anger is not criminal unless Niko used detention to advance it.
concede: His admission connects the employment demand directly to release.
burden_drift: A serious grievance can make me assume he planned coercion from the start.
burden_correct: The first safety lock was lawful; only the later conduct is charged.
final: The admitted condition proves that continued detention served Niko’s demand.

jurors.label: Retired paramedic
jurors.persona: Initially gives emergency judgment broad latitude but insists that emergency authority must end.

agree: Sheltering during the original warning was a reasonable safety response.
pushback: At 4:18 the emergency ended; at 4:19 Niko made a different choice.
concede: The one-minute sequence separates caution from coercion for me.
burden_drift: Once the warning cleared, I want Niko to explain why he knew better than security.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove his choice was knowing and conditional, not merely mistaken.
final: The later local hold and repeated demand satisfy that burden.

jurors.label: Building manager
jurors.persona: Knows access records are precise about control but cautious about what they reveal about intention.

agree: The personal code proves Niko continued the restriction after the release signal.
pushback: The access system cannot read his purpose, so I need the spoken condition too.
concede: The recording supplies the intention that the access log cannot contain.
burden_drift: A personal code can feel like personal guilt before the purpose is proved.
burden_correct: The records must support every element rather than substitute for them.
final: Control and intention are independently proved and then corroborate each other.

jurors.label: Community mediator
jurors.persona: Distinguishes an emotional demand from coercion by asking what leverage made refusal impossible.

agree: A demand becomes coercive here because Leda’s release was the leverage.
pushback: Niko’s anger alone cannot prove hostage-taking.
concede: His own admission removes doubt about the condition he imposed.
burden_drift: The director’s refusal makes me want to judge Niko for the entire dispute.
burden_correct: We are deciding detention and compulsion, not whether the investigation was fair.
final: The prosecution proved the precise unlawful leverage required by the charge.

jurors.label: Audio editor
jurors.persona: Trusts complete contemporaneous recordings more than remembered summaries or isolated phrases.

agree: The phone recording preserves Leda’s question and Niko’s condition in sequence.
pushback: The isolated phrase ‘I am staying’ leaves out who controlled the door.
concede: The matching timestamp and access record answer my concern about context.
burden_drift: A clear recording can make me stop testing how the file was preserved.
burden_correct: The file still needs authentication and must prove the charged condition.
final: The authenticated recording supports guilt without relying on memory alone.

jurors.label: Hospital receptionist
jurors.persona: Understands cautious messages from people who feel watched and resists judging their wording in isolation.

agree: Leda’s cautious first message is consistent with trying not to provoke Niko.
pushback: Her word ‘staying’ does not answer whether the choice was voluntary.
concede: I accept that the original warning gave everyone a valid reason to shelter.
burden_drift: Leda’s fear makes me want to accept her interpretation without checking it.
burden_correct: Her account must still match the door record, recording, and director’s evidence.
final: Those independent sources confirm that Leda was detained for leverage.

jurors.label: Café owner and foreperson
jurors.persona: Keeps the room focused on the transition from emergency protection to employment leverage.

agree: The case turns on what Niko chose after the central warning ended.
pushback: We should not treat the entire incident as one undivided emergency.
concede: The local hold, demand, and recording form a single later sequence.
burden_drift: The seriousness of captivity can make the room skip Niko’s knowledge element.
burden_correct: We must find intentional detention, a release condition, and knowledge beyond reasonable doubt.
final: Each element is proved by a different source, and the sources agree.
